processes.process: Aluminium (primary) Global average
processes.note: Aluminium (primary), global average. Chosen as the default over the European route on evidence, not on fit: GARO's own LCA report lists supplier transport routes spanning Poland, Germany, Czech Republic, Italy, Turkey, China, Denmark and Slovenia -- a genuinely international supplier base, not a predominantly Nordic one -- and no source (the LCA report, GARO's 2025 sustainability report, or GARO's public materials) names a specific smelter, grid, or bauxite origin for the aluminium itself. Absent that evidence, assuming clean Nordic/European primary smelting is the less defensible default, not the more defensible one. This also happens to sit closer to the published study's own aluminium factor than the European route would -- see model.py:validate_against_published -- but that agreement is a consequence of the evidence-based choice, not the reason for making it.

processes.process: Aluminium (secondary)
processes.note: Aluminium (secondary). The recycled-content lever now moves between two real production processes rather than between two reporting factors.

processes.process: Aluminium  recycling credit closed loop (79% virgin part trade mix)
processes.note: Closed-loop recycling credit, negative by construction. Used only under the substitution allocation convention.

processes.process: Rolling aluminium sheet
processes.note: Rolling aluminium sheet, as a stand-in for enclosure and pedestal forming.

processes.process: Aluminium (primary) European production, bauxite from Africa
processes.note: Aluminium (primary), European production. Kept as a labelled comparison point, not the default, precisely because it is the reading a reviewer would expect from the factory's Swedish location and would be wrong to assume without supplier evidence. Used in the validation reconciliation to show how much of the model's result depends on this one choice.

processes.process: Steel virgin + 15% scrap BOF for beams & sheet
processes.note: Steel virgin + 15% scrap BOF, beams and sheet. The BOF route is the virgin end of the recycled-content lever.

processes.process: Steel from 100% scrap EAF for beams & sheet
processes.note: Steel from 100% scrap EAF. The EAF route is the fully secondary end.

processes.process: Steel  recycling credit closed loop (50.2% virgin part in trade mix)
processes.note: Steel closed-loop recycling credit.

processes.process: Copper rod tube plate (primary)
processes.note: Copper rod/tube/plate (primary). The charging cable conductor.

processes.process: Copper (secondary)
processes.note: Copper (secondary).

processes.process: Copper  recycling credit closed loop (45% virgin part in trade mix)
processes.note: Copper closed-loop recycling credit.

processes.process: ABS (Acrylonitrile butadiene styrene)
processes.note: ABS. The published study reports a generic 'Plastics' category; ABS is the closest engineering polymer Idemat resolves and is the usual choice for this enclosure class. PC/ABS blends would sit between this and A.130.07.109 (PC).

processes.process: rABS - mechanical recycled in China - ex transport
processes.note: rABS, mechanically recycled. Mechanical rather than chemical recycling, which is what a housing recyclate stream realistically is.

processes.process: ABS closed loop chemical upcycling credit
processes.note: ABS closed-loop upcycling credit.

processes.process: ABS (Acrylonitrile butadiene styrene) waste incineration with electricity
processes.note: ABS waste incineration with electricity recovery. Carries the energy-recovery credit in its CED term, which is why CED goes negative here.

processes.process: Synthetic average: PCB of refrigerator + PCB of washing machine
processes.note: Not a single Idemat database entry: no process represents a charging-station metering/RCD board, so this is the arithmetic mean of the two closest available analogues, both mains-voltage white-goods control boards -- A.050.06.304 (PCB of refrigerator) and A.050.06.305 (PCB of washing machine), constructed by circuopt.idemat.average_process(). Averaging across the available evidence rather than pinning one arbitrarily follows the same logic as the aluminium process choice. Both source processes explicitly exclude integrated circuits (ICs), which the underlying Idemat category names state directly -- a real limitation of this proxy that the averaging does not resolve, and which is why this remains the weakest mapping in the model and the family perturbed hardest in the scenario ensemble.

processes.process: landfill (inert waste)
processes.note: Landfill, inert waste. Zero across all indicators in Idemat, which is itself a modelling limitation worth stating rather than hiding: it means landfill is penalised only through the loss of the recycling credit, not through a burden of its own.

processes.process: Scrap collection&sorting (copper)
processes.note: Scrap collection and sorting (copper), used as the generic separate-collection burden for all recovered streams.

processes.process: Metals open loop recycling credit
processes.note: Metals open-loop recycling credit. Zero in Idemat by convention: downcycled metal earns no credit.

processes.process: Plastics open loop recycling credit
processes.note: Plastics open-loop recycling credit. Also zero by convention.

geography_reconciliation.note: The model defaults to the global-average primary aluminium route because GARO's own LCA report shows an internationally distributed supplier base and names no specific smelter for the aluminium itself -- an evidence-based choice, made before checking whether it would improve agreement with the published figure. That it also sits closer to the published study's own aluminium factor than the European route would is a consequence of that choice, not the reason for it. The European route is shown here as a labelled alternative: using it instead would move the model further from the published figure, not closer.

E7_parameters.verdict: The interior optimum is a property of the assumed penalty parameters, not an empirical result: it appears in 22 of 27 corner combinations.

E12_validation_decomposition.verdict: 12% of the family-level disagreement cancels in the total, so the aggregate agreement overstates the model's per-material accuracy.

E13_electronics.verdict: Electronics would have to be roughly 8.3x its current factor before it overtakes aluminium as the largest material contributor -- a far larger error than the scenario ensemble's own perturbation of this factor. Across the tested range the archive's ranking barely moves regardless (worst-case Spearman +0.933) because electronics mass is not a decision variable -- scaling its factor shifts every design's score together.

E14_prices.note: World Bank has no directly comparable steel-scrap entry (it publishes iron ore, a different commodity), so this test covers aluminium and copper only.

E15_spread.verdict: Ranked by how much each moves the Planet objective: grid region (6 European markets) (201.9) > inventory backend (Idemat vs DEFRA) (57.8) > design choice (whole Pareto archive) (7.3) > allocation convention (cut-off vs substitution) (2.3)
